title: Ethiopian Coffee with Butter
community: Oromo and some highland communities — the butter coffee tradition
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Coffee with Butter — strong Ethiopian coffee brewed in the jebena and served with a small piece of fresh butter melted in. The highland farming tradition — butter coffee predates the global 'bulletproof coffee' trend by centuries in Ethiopia's Oromo communities.
longDesc: Coffee with butter is the highland farmer's breakfast coffee — the fat from the butter sustains energy through the morning's physical work. The Oromo communities have been adding butter to coffee for generations, long before the concept became global.
ingredients: 1 tsp fresh unsalted butter per cup
Salt to taste (Harrar and some Oromo communities add salt not sugar)
steps: Brew strong Ethiopian coffee as per ETH212.
Add a small piece of fresh butter to each cup.
Add salt if following the traditional salted version.
The butter melts as you drink — stir or swirl.
chefTips: Fresh, high-quality butter is essential — the fat is the point.
Traditional versions use salt, not sugar.
commonMistakes: Blending — traditional coffee with butter is not blended.
cookingScience: The fat in butter dissolves the fat-soluble aromatic compounds in coffee (particularly the cafestol and kahweol diterpenes) — enhancing the coffee's body and producing a smoother, less bitter experience. The fat also slows caffeine absorption, producing more sustained energy release.
sustainabilityTips: Ethiopian highland butter — from grass-fed cattle.
healthBenefits: Butter fat supports sustained energy release.
The fat-soluble coffee compounds (diterpenes) have documented anti-cancer properties.
culturalNote: Ethiopian coffee with butter predates the global butter coffee trend by centuries — the Oromo highland farmer who has been starting their day with butter in their jebena coffee since long before the internet had no idea they were ahead of a global trend. This is traditional food knowledge from the world's oldest coffee culture.
